company: Original 1971 'Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory' screen props (seller Dan, Los Angeles)
product: Pawn Stars clip 'Original 1971 "Willy Wonka" Props (Season 14)' (YouTube id 94i2e2K7Fns, Pawn Stars official channel, episode 'La La Land'). Rick goes to L.A. Collection of five props: Gene Wilder's hat, golden egg, golden ticket, wooden Wonka bars, Everlasting Gobstopper. Asking $725,000 for the collection. Rick buys the Gobstopper plus one Wonka bar for $105,000.

facts.fact: Seller: five props from the original 1971 film; asking price for the collection is $725,000.
Hat is the original hat Gene Wilder wore in the film; Rick tries it on and jokes about Wilder's small head.
Golden egg, screen-used golden ticket, Wonka bars made of wood ('they still haven't melted').
Bought at auction; every prop came from Julie Dawn Cole, who played Veruca Salt.
Everlasting Gobstopper; Rick: 'like the Hope Diamond', 'like the Holy Grail'; he remembers it from age seven.
Movie was a flop in theaters, became a cult classic after home video in the 80s.

Negotiation: seller sticks with $100,000 for the Gobstopper alone; Rick asks to throw in a Wonka bar; seller offers bar + Gobstopper for $115,000; Rick asks for $100,000, seller says no; Rick offers $105,000 with a Wonka bar; deal.
facts.source: broadcast transcript ids 68-84; on-screen tags $100,000 / now $100,000 / now $105,000; https://www.looper.com/362966/the-two-willy-wonka-props-that-sold-for-more-than-100k-on-pawn-stars ; https://blaze.tv/series/pawn-stars/pawn-stars-biggest-ever-deals

facts.fact: Rick: 'I'm seven years old again'; plans to put the props in the shop to bring people in.
No confirmed record found of a later resale of this Gobstopper.
